What is the domain of the function f(x)=2cot⁡(3x)? Assume that n is an integer.

decision.explanation: Cotangent is undefined when its sine denominator is zero. Thus sin(3x) ≠ 0 requires 3x ≠ nπ, so x ≠ nπ/3 for every integer n.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: What is the domain of the function  $f(x)=2\operatorname{cot}⁡(3x)?$ Assume that $n$ is an integer.
after.worked_solution:
The domain of $y=\operatorname{cot}⁡x$ is given by the expression

$$
x\ne n\pi ,
$$

where $n$ is an integer.

To find the domain of $2\operatorname{cot}⁡(3x),$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $(3x).$ This gives

$$
3x\ne n\pi .
$$

Solving for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3x & \ne n\pi  \\ x & \ne \frac{n\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the domain of the function is $x\ne \frac{n\pi }{3},$ where $n$ is an integer.

Which of the following expressions gives all of the vertical asymptotes of the function f(x)=tan⁡(3x)+2? Assume that n is an integer.

a
x=π6+nπ3
b
x=π6+nπ2
c
x=π4+π2
d
x=π2+nπ3
e
x=π3+nπ3
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The asymptotes of y=tan⁡x are given by the expression

x=π2+nπ, where n is an integer.

To find the asymptotes of tan⁡(3x)+2, we replace the x on the left-hand side of the above with (3x). This gives

3x=π2+nπ.

Solving for x, we get

3x=π2+nπx=π6+nπ3.

Therefore, we conclude that the expression giving all the vertical asymptotes is x=π6+nπ3, where n is an integer.

content.problem: Which of the following expressions gives all of the vertical asymptotes of the function $f(x)=\operatorname{tan}⁡(3x)+2?$ Assume that $n$ is an integer.
content.worked_solution:
The asymptotes of $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡x$ are given by the expression

$$
x=\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi ,
$$

where $n$ is an integer.

To find the asymptotes of $\operatorname{tan}⁡(3x)+2,$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $(3x).$ This gives

$$
3x=\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi .
$$

Solving for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3x & =\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{\pi }{6}+\frac{n\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the expression giving all the vertical asymptotes is $x=\frac{\pi }{6}+\frac{n\pi }{3},$ where $n$ is an integer.

content.problem: Which of the following expressions gives all of the zeros of the function $f(x)=\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x)?$ Assume that $n$ is an integer.
content.worked_solution:
The zeros of $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡x$ are given by

$$
x=n\pi ,
$$

where $n$ is an integer.

To find the zeros of $f(x)=\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x),$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $(2x).$ This gives

$$
2x=n\pi .
$$

Solving for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & =n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{n\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the zeros are $x=\frac{n\pi }{2},$ where $n$ is an integer.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem: Which of the following expressions gives all of the vertical asymptotes of the function $f(x)=\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{\pi x}{2})?$ Assume that $n$ is an integer.
after.worked_solution:
The asymptotes of $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡x$ are given by the expression

$$
x=\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi ,
$$

where $n$ is an integer.

To find the asymptotes of $\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{\pi x}{2}),$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $(\frac{\pi x}{2}).$ This gives

$$
\frac{\pi x}{2}=\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi .
$$

Solving for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\pi x}{2} & =\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi  \\ \frac{x}{2} & =\frac{1}{2}+n \\ x & =1+2n.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the expression giving all the vertical asymptotes is $x=1+2n,$ where $n$ is an integer.
